title: Birthday Kaomoji (*^▽^)/🎂: Copy & Paste Party Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste birthday kaomoji: cake faces (*^▽^)/🎂, cheering ٩(ˊᗜˋ*)و, party poppers (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ🎉, presents (づ￣ ³￣)づ🎁 and a beer toast (^_^)/□☆□\(^_^).
hero_tagline: One-line birthday faces with cake, candles, party poppers and gifts, sized to drop into a message or under a photo. Tap one to copy it.
intro: A birthday kaomoji is a single line, so it goes straight into a text, a comment or a group chat without breaking the layout. The face does the celebrating and an emoji or two carries the object: 🎂 for the cake, 🕯️ for a candle, 🎉 for the party popper. Some symbols do the job in text alone: □ is a beer mug in the toast (^_^)/□☆□\(^_^), and ڡ, an Arabic letter, curls out of a mouth like a tongue licking icing. For a multi-line cake or a big HAPPY BIRTHDAY banner built from characters, use the birthday ASCII art page linked below; this page keeps to faces that fit on one line. ꒰, ꒱ and ᗜ come from Yi and Canadian syllabics, so a device without those fonts shows a box in their place.

faq.q: What is the difference between birthday kaomoji and birthday ASCII art?
faq.a: A kaomoji is one line: a face plus maybe an emoji, like (*^▽^)/🎂, so it fits anywhere a word fits. Birthday ASCII art stacks several lines to draw a whole cake or banner and needs a place that keeps line breaks.
Two people toasting. Each □ is a mug held up in a raised arm, and ☆ in the middle is the clink. It is a common Japanese kaomoji for cheers, used at birthdays, parties and after good news.

faq.q: Can I make a birthday cake kaomoji without emoji?
faq.a: Yes, though the cake itself is hard to draw on one line. Faces like (っ˘ڡ˘ς), where ڡ is a tongue licking the lips, or the toast (^_^)/□☆□\(^_^) carry the party feeling with text characters only.
